en: The Hymn to Śākyasiṃha composed by Viṣṇu. Om. Homage to the Omniscient One!
O Śrīghana, you whose nature is eternal bliss, I am your devotee;
you are the bridge across the ocean of existence, the radiant cause of liberation,
the ordainer of the three realms, and the protector who grants supreme security.
I bow to the state of Buddhahood—well-skilled, with beautiful flanks, well-born, and perfectly self-controlled;
possessing the great virtues of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, meditative concentration, and vigor; and having reached the further shore of supreme knowledge.
He who uplifts the world through the four modes of Brahma-abiding, who teaches the Dharma of the Four Truths, and who is beautifully adorned.
In a forest that is easy to traverse, radiant, and most delightful, where even the king of gods and others may go,
he sat upon his fourth seat, bestowing [teachings] for the sake of the welfare of beings.
He who has established the world in a state of well-being and stands ready for its protection.
I bow to him who possesses great vigor, who conquers the world of the four Māras, who laughs at the triple net and Time,
whose body is armored with patience, and who is the abode of liberation.
Likewise, [he praised] the sole lord of the three worlds, the Lord of the Śākyas. || 4 ||
Surely he by whom the entire army of Māra was conquered— without weapons and without allies—
was one who wore patience as armor and held the bow of loving-kindness.
By him who stood at the Bodhi tree in order to protect the world. || 5 ||
One whose body and home shine with cool features, who is full of affection toward people and possesses a home even in the forest,
and who is endowed with thirty-two marks known as *lakṣaṇas*— [he is a Bodhisattva].
Extremely difficult to attain within the three realms of existence, it is honored by the world.
"May I become a protector in this Kali age, which is bereft of a lord, remaining well-established in the Dharmamegha [stage] of meditation.
Thus he made his vow to protect himself.
He was born in the Śākya lineage, the crest-jewel of the earth-protectors.
Your vision is obtained through fortune; likewise, the intellect of those possessed of fortune approaches you of its own accord.
While you remain amidst the cloud of Dharma, how could there be [any other] vision?
Being deprived [of that], they are not capable of entering there. || 8 ||
Now, by the mass of dust arisen from the lotus-feet of your honor, the three worlds have been purified;
likewise, our heads have truly become pure.
I shall pursue enlightenment through your teaching, O Bhava. || 9 ||
Whoever, standing before the Jina, constantly recites this *Bhujaṅgaprayāta* composed by Mādhava,
shall always have auspiciousness in his home and in his excellent body.
And the Buddhas, being pleased, will provide protection. || 10 ||
Having severed the triple net and likewise enjoyed all pleasures, and having reached the further shore of generosity, ethical conduct, and the other perfections,
they attained great enlightenment and protect the world.
And in the end, they shall go to that which is called Sukhāvatī.
The *Bhujaṅgaprayāta* hymn composed by Viṣṇu to the illustrious Śākyasiṃha is completed.
